target_customer: Mobile AR and game developers needing shared, multiplayer AR experiences
problem: ARKit and ARCore gave single user AR, so developers lacked backend services for multiplayer, persistent and cross platform AR.
business_model: Usage based developer API (planned); acquired before scaling revenue

founders.name: Ross Finman
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in Niantic's acquisition announcement (as quoted by search coverage). The YC page lists no founders. Background not confirmed in an opened source.

founders.name: Diana Hu
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in Niantic's announcement; CB Insights calls her co-founder and CTO. Education not confirmed in an opened source.

competitors.name: Apple ARKit
competitors.what: Single user AR SDK for iOS
competitors.traction_then: Announced mid 2017; lacked shared multi user experiences

competitors.name: Google ARCore
competitors.what: Single user AR SDK for Android
competitors.traction_then: Lacked shared experiences until Cloud Anchors in ARCore 1.2

technical_complexity.rationale: Shared, persistent AR needs real time computer vision relocalization across devices and backend sync, research grade for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Hard computer vision and backend work, but platform owners could ship multiplayer into their own SDKs, as Google did with Cloud Anchors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google added Cloud Anchors in 2018; Niantic bought the company in February 2018 and folded the technology into its Real World Platform.

market_need_then: Pokemon Go style games and the ARKit and ARCore launches in 2017 made AR developers want shared worlds, which the platform SDKs did not yet provide.

rebrands.why: Not stated; CB Insights lists the earlier name, date unknown.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage beyond acquisition news; the Escher name was shared with the artist and other companies.

outcome_analysis: Escher Reality was a two person team building a multiplayer AR backend during the 2017 ARKit and ARCore launches. Backed by Uncork, Founders Fund and YC, it was acquired by Niantic on 1 February 2018 for an undisclosed price, with some outlets calling it an acquihire. The wedge of shared AR was real but platform owners were moving into it, so the exit came before a standalone business formed.
notes: No company website exists in the directory. Funding amount unknown: CB Insights lists 120K over 5 rounds, aggregator only. Founder names come from search results quoting Niantic's blog; the Niantic page itself redirected and then returned 404, and the YC page lists no founders. An archive site claims the founders met at Carnegie Mellon, unverified. Competitors 6D.ai and Ubiquity6 appear only in 2018 and later coverage so are not listed.
